rewrites.summary:
Tabasco has enacted no legal procedure for recognising gender identity. A Human Rights Watch report co-produced with a local inclusion centre (March 2024) documented that the absence of any recognition procedure leaves trans people's identity documents permanently mismatched and exposed to police and institutional mistreatment.

By March 2025, Human Rights Watch counted 22 of Mexico's 32 states as having legislated legal gender recognition and named six — among them Tabasco, the subject of the dedicated 2024 report — whose legislatures had enacted none. For a visible trans visitor the document mismatch is the practical trigger: an ID that does not match presentation invites the questioning and mistreatment the report records.

rewrites.summary:
Quebec's recorded profile rests on the national data series: Statistics Canada's March 2026 release on police-reported hate crime (2024 data) shows gender-identity/expression-motivated incidents rising nationally for a fourth consecutive year — +8% to 139, nearly triple 2020 — and identifies no trans-specific provincial pattern for Quebec.

No Quebec-specific anti-trans legislation, ordinance or incident series appears in the surviving sources, alongside national NGO analysis of the same police data; the province's largest city anchors one of the country's most established organised 2SLGBTQ+ communities.
